A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DisBack study. Their main text, equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation evaluations, convergence and mismatch experiments, ablations, Gaussian-mixture simulations, and a user preference study.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds EDM-to-FastGAN experiments, checkpoint sensitivity tests, mismatch diagnostics, and failure examples.

M1.justification: The degradation-recording and distribution-backtracking procedures, alternating updates, and training objectives remain unchanged in Section 4. The FastGAN experiment applies the existing method to another student architecture without introducing a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: The image-generation, text-to-image, and Gaussian-mixture coverage is retained. CelebA, newly receiving quantitative results in v3 Table 5, was already explicitly described as an experimental dataset in v1 Appendix B.1. Additional architecture and sensitivity experiments do not establish new task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v3 substantially expands corresponding comparisons: ImageNet gains CTM, DMD2, Sid, DDDM, BOOT, SlimFlow, and Moment Matching; text-to-image evaluation gains LCM-SDXL, DMD2, SDXL-Turbo, and SDXL Lightning. Table 5 additionally compares against FastGAN and Score GAN. These are reported comparisons, including methods previously only cited.

E3.justification: The main experiments change from separately reported EDM/CD initializations to EDM teachers, while Appendix B.2 changes the stated EDM training budget from 500,000 epochs to 50,000 iterations. Convergence comparisons now include degradation overhead. New experiments introduce FastGAN students, Patch-FID/CLIP/IS metrics, noise-scale comparisons, and checkpoint/degradation settings. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained trajectory-removal ablation and two-dimensional demonstrations, v3 adds intermediate-teacher visualizations, generated-versus-training-data mismatch diagnostics across noise levels, checkpoint-count and degradation-length sensitivity tests, and explicit failure cases (Appendices A.3, E.1, G, and H). These substantially expand scrutiny of the proposed mechanism and its failure conditions.

E5.justification: Both versions display standard deviations in Figure 4 and retain the same user-study aggregation. v3 introduces no documented change to repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance testing, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v3 reports ImageNet FID 1.38, replacing v1's separately reported 8.44 EDM and 5.73 CD results under revised settings; this is not an established same-setting gain. Figure 1 revises speedups, including CIFAR10 from 13.09x to 5.67x. Tables 4–6 add extensive metric, FastGAN, and sensitivity results, although Appendix G's numerical prose disagrees with Table 6.

T1.justification: Theorem 1, the KL-gradient and Stable Target Field derivations in Appendix C, and the vector-field assumption remain substantively unchanged. Equation 9 makes sampling notation explicit, and the added KL objective restates existing mathematics; neither establishes a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain trajectory-constrained distillation, faster convergence, competitive generation quality, and compatibility with existing distillation methods. Highlighting FID 1.38 in v3's abstract supplies new evidence for the existing performance claim; comparable-or-better quality was already claimed in v1's conclusion.

C2.justification: v3 distinguishes auxiliary-model mismatch from teacher-model mismatch and explains how initialization addresses the former (Appendix D.2). Appendices G and H add substantive explanations of excessive degradation, checkpoint scheduling problems, unclear backgrounds, and failures of global structure. These considerably develop v1's more general hyperparameter and teacher-dependence limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 revises training-budget and pretrained-model information and removes the separate CD-training recipe. Appendix A also drops v1's explicit LAION-Aesthetic-6.5+ training-subset specification for LCM-LoRA. Most optimizer, hardware, checkpoint-schedule, and public-code information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused discussion distinguishing DisBack's mismatch problem from DLSM and TIW-DSM. References also expand for newly compared methods and proposed future architectures, while the existing diffusion-distillation positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v3 edits the title, affiliations, abstract, and explanatory prose, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes the expanded appendices into additional subsections. The main section sequence and central narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: The main benchmark table is split into unconditional and conditional comparisons, the text-to-image table gains methods and metrics, and new appendix tables are added. Convergence plots are redrawn to show overhead; trajectory, gradient, mismatch, and failure illustrations are added. The LCM-LoRA image comparison is condensed and moved into the main text.

improvement.justification: Broader comparisons, overhead-inclusive speed reporting, and checkpoint and failure analyses make v3 more informative and better expose limitations than v1. The net improvement is constrained by reporting inconsistencies: Appendix G disagrees with Table 6, and Appendix A.1 retains a 1.5x speedup while Figure 7 shows 1.36x. Revised teacher configurations and training budgets also prevent interpreting the lower headline FID as a verified same-setting improvement.
